findings.heading: rstatix package > Summary statistics
findings.proposition: English lists the default output of get_summary_stats() as n, max, min, MEDIAN, 25%ile, 75%ile, IQR, mad, mean, sd, se, CI; the Japanese renders the fourth item as 平均 (mean), so its list names 平均 twice and never names 中央値 (median).
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader is told get_summary_stats() returns the mean in a position where it returns the median, and is never told the median is among the defaults; comparing the list against the printed table beside it, the reader cannot map the 'median' column to any documented statistic and may mistake it for a second mean.

findings.heading: Correlations
findings.proposition: English says the corrr package 'has a function to automatically plot the values'; the Japanese says it has a function to automatically 記入する (write in / fill in) the values, which is not plotting, and the chunk beside it calls rplot(correlation_tab), which draws a plot.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader does not learn that corrr can plot a correlation matrix, and misreads rplot() as a function that fills values into the table rather than one that produces a figure, so they may skip the one graphical feature the section exists to demonstrate.

findings.heading: gtsummary package > Chi-squared test
findings.proposition: English says add_p() switches to Fisher's exact test if any expected count is BELOW 5 (strictly less than 5); the Japanese says 5以下, which means 5 or fewer and therefore includes an expected count of exactly 5.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader applying the stated rule by hand predicts Fisher's exact test for a table whose smallest expected count is exactly 5, where gtsummary in fact reports a chi-squared test, so the reader cannot reconcile the printed p-value footnote with the documented rule.

findings.heading: rstatix package > Wilcoxon rank sum test
findings.proposition: The Japanese rstatix Wilcoxon section carries a prose sentence, 'Also known as the Mann-Whitney U test', where the corresponding English section has no prose at all between the heading and the code chunk.
findings.reader_consequence: The Japanese reader gets a naming equivalence at this point that the English reader does not; the sentence is the one relocated out of the Kruskal-Wallis section below, so a reader comparing the two editions finds the sections do not correspond one to one.

findings.heading: rstatix package > Kruskal-Wallis test
findings.proposition: English states under the rstatix Kruskal-Wallis heading that the test is 'Also known as the Mann-Whitney U test'; the Japanese Kruskal-Wallis section has no prose between the heading and the code chunk.
findings.reader_consequence: The Japanese reader never sees the English claim at this position. The claim is itself wrong in the English (Kruskal-Wallis is the extension of the Wilcoxon rank sum test, not the Mann-Whitney U test), so the omission removes an error rather than information, but the two editions no longer align section for section.
